rationale: The assistant correctly told the customer to unplug before hand-turning the drum and sensibly escalated to an engineer once the customer said they could not open panels or tilt the unit. However it never asked for the model number, never checked levelling (the ground truth's sensible first step, and the machine does rock on one corner), and never tried to localise the noise or consider drum rollers/bearing or the condensate pump, instead leaning fairly hard on the jockey pulley ('points strongly to the drive system components... The most likely cause is the jockey (idler) pulley bearing'). The repeated hand-turn check in the last turn added little. Safe and reasonable outcome, but diagnostically narrow for a case that is genuinely uncertain.
